X.note: Same 3D-render setup as Y, but the crowd reads better. Figures are distinct: white-uniformed sailors, khaki soldiers, a stack of barrels or tyres and carried boxes. Colours and uniforms look plausible, so it feels like a staged scene. The figures are still stiff, small and mannequin-like. The Union Jack in the distance is only a few pixels wide. Plaster and cobbles look good.

Y.note: The crowd is a cluster of olive-green and blue clay-like figures with smeared faces and ambiguous poses. The figures merge into a blob and look like game or clay assets. The buildings are the same strong 3D render. Their weathering is slightly busier and more patchy, which looks a bit more arbitrary. The uniforms are unconvincing.

why: The buildings and harbour backdrop are near-identical, but X's crowd is more readable, varied and uniform-plausible, while Y's figures look like melted clay dolls.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the clay-like crowd with fewer, larger, properly modelled figures in period uniforms (khaki battledress, white naval tropical kit). Give them distinct poses and cast shadows, and separate them so they don't merge into one mass.
anachronisms_seen: No clear anachronisms in either frame
Uniforms in Y are generic and ambiguous rather than clearly 1943 British
Union Jack is too tiny to verify
